html:
Sapa Inca, or emperor, of the Inca Empire from 1493 to about 1527, when it was at its largest. He was the son of Topa Inca Yupanqui.

He pushed the frontier north into what are now Ecuador and southern Colombia and spent many years there, fighting and building, around Tomebamba and Quito. The empire then ran some 4,000 kilometres along the Andes.

Around 1527 an epidemic, most likely smallpox, spread into the empire from the Spanish colonies to the north, ahead of the Spanish themselves. It killed Huayna Capac and the son he had chosen as heir.

Two other sons then claimed the throne: Huáscar in Cusco and Atahualpa in the north. Their civil war tore the empire apart. Atahualpa had just won when Francisco Pizarro arrived, and the Spanish seized him at Cajamarca in 1532.
sum: Sapa Inca, or emperor, of the Inca Empire from 1493 to about 1527, when it was at its largest. He was the son of Topa Inca Yupanqui.
